claims.statement: A RunTree models a root trace or child run with per-run id and parent_run_id, while all ordinary descendants inherit the root trace_id and extend the parent's dotted_order with a timestamp-plus-UUID segment.

Both SDKs generate absent run IDs as UUID v7 values derived from start time; JavaScript uses an execution-order tie breaker and Python prevents an explicitly supplied child start time from preceding its parent.

Batch and multipart ingestion depend on trace_id and dotted_order: JavaScript rejects multipart creates or updates missing either field, while Python uses their presence to select its queue/compressed batch create path.
Trace sampling is keyed consistently by trace_id, with the root dotted_order segment and then run id used as fallbacks.

RunTree child creation preserves root trace identity, the parent's selected project-or-address destination and client, merges parent metadata with child keys taking precedence, extends dotted_order, and appends the child to the in-memory child list; tracing wrappers assemble inherited tags before child creation.

JavaScript traceable nesting propagates the current run through AsyncLocalStorage and snapshots context for async iterator and stream continuations; Python uses copied contextvars contexts and stores the active parent as a weak reference to avoid retention by captured asyncio contexts.

Distributed tracing exports the full dotted_order in langsmith-trace and annotations plus the selected project or address in baggage; import reconstructs trace_id from the first segment and run id from the last so receiving code can create a child in the same trace, with Python also restoring the immediate parent_run_id when present.

Replica routing parsed from untrusted baggage is filtered to header-safe routing fields and does not accept credentials, endpoints, or client objects; Python additionally filters replica update keys through a fail-closed allow-list that always retains the reroot key.

Run persistence is a start-post followed by in-memory end and completion patch, and patch updates exclude inputs by default so batching cannot overwrite create inputs during create/update merging; JavaScript omits the key directly and Python passes None so the client update builder omits it.

JavaScript traceable async iterators complete on exhaustion with aggregated chunks, record and rethrow iterator errors, and on early termination call the source iterator return method, mark the run Cancelled, preserve partial outputs, and skip waiting for unfinished children.
JavaScript ReadableStream tracing completes when the tapped reader is exhausted and explicitly records Cancelled with partial chunks before forwarding cancellation to the source reader.
For JavaScript non-stream values and promises, synchronous throws become rejected promises, completion records the error and rethrows it, and error paths avoid waiting for unfinished child runs.

Python traceable wrappers finalize and rethrow BaseException for sync, async, generator, and async-generator paths; async error cleanup is shielded from cancellation, and generator completion includes chunks accumulated before failure or close.

Python returned stream wrappers defer trace completion until exhaustion or context-manager exit and best-effort finalize on destruction; synchronous iteration records exceptions, while the asynchronous __aiter__ and __aexit__ finalization paths currently do not pass the triggering exception to trace finalization.

Attachments are binary sidecars removed from ordinary inputs; Python extracts Attachment-annotated arguments and rejects filesystem-backed or ambiguous attachment values unless dangerously_allow_filesystem is explicitly enabled.

Replica routing preserves IDs for a primary destination and deterministically remaps id, parent_run_id, trace_id, and every dotted_order UUID suffix for secondary project or address destinations. Both SDKs can slice ancestry at a distributed-parent marker; JavaScript can additionally make the current run a root without that marker and tracks the replica-specific root for descendants, whereas Python's current reroot update acts only when the distributed marker exists.

Python groups replicas that produce identical payload bytes for shared serialization and supports a dedicated client per replica, while JavaScript strips reroot when children inherit replica configuration so reroot applies only where explicitly configured.

A run is routed to either a project or a validated agent address, never both at one precedence level; an active or distributed parent supplies the complete inherited destination, while root wrappers choose the first named project-or-address tier instead of conflating an address with a project name.

Agent addresses have the form lrn:agents/{id}/environments/{environment}, validate the agent ID as a lowercase DNS label and normalize one of four environments to lowercase; malformed explicit values raise, while an invalid deciding environment configuration disables that trace with a warning instead of breaking wrapped application code, and unsupported workspaces reject addressed runs without project fallback.

Distributed destination baggage is fail-closed: valid upstream project or address routing outranks caller routing, but a parent naming both is rejected; invalid addresses and malformed replicas are ignored, and attacker-controlled values are not echoed in warnings.

Current JavaScript and Python baggage serializers emit metadata, tags, and project or address but do not emit replica configuration, although their parsers still accept langsmith-replicas for compatibility.

Python tracing_context snapshots the prior tracing context, optionally imports a parent from headers or dotted order, merges inherited annotations, installs project/address and distributed-parent state for the block, and restores the complete previous context in a finally block.

JavaScript ReadableStream tracing records source-read errors with partial chunks before rethrowing, while explicit cancellation records Cancelled with partial chunks before forwarding cancellation to the source reader; normal exhaustion completes with all accumulated chunks.

JavaScript currently drains synchronous generators eagerly, completes tracing from the collected results, and returns a replaying generator, so later consumer-side early termination cannot cancel the already-drained producer.

Python moves Attachment values out of JSON inputs into binary sidecars, records uploaded attachment names after posting, and filters already-uploaded tuple attachments from completion patches to avoid duplicate upload.
